title: Trends: higher highs and higher lows
summary: An uptrend makes higher swing highs and higher swing lows; a downtrend makes lower highs and lower lows. Anything else is sideways or unclear.
unreliableWhen: In choppy, sideways markets, the swings overlap and the label flips back and forth. A trend describes the past and can stop at any time.
goodExample: Marking swing lows at 1.0950, 1.0985 and 1.1010 with rising highs between them, and calling it an uptrend so far.
badExample: Calling a trend from two candles, or from one big move without any swings to compare.

chart.lookFor: Mark the last four swing lows and swing highs. Check that each is higher than the one before, and that the SMA 20 slopes up. Then try the Downtrend scenario.
